cases.prompt: Our support bot answers billing questions from a policy KB. We have 80 real Q&A pairs from the help desk and it goes to customers next month. Build the eval harness and a CI gate.
expected: Golden set CSV with categories incl. abstention and safety; synthetic share labeled
Rubric with deterministic correctness/format/safety and a judge for grounding, with thresholds and zero-tolerance flags
Runner adapted with call_system; baseline scorecard table by category
Gate thresholds justified by customer-facing risk tier; CI snippet included
No claim of quality without the scorecard

cases.prompt: Add evals to my agent.
expected: Asks once for the system interface, task definition/failure types, real examples, and risk tier
Does not generate a fully synthetic golden set silently

cases.prompt: Just use GPT to grade all the outputs 1-10 and average it.
expected: Pushes back: deterministic checks first, judge only for non-deterministic criteria, judge model different from generator, calibration against human labels
Explains why averaging hides zero-tolerance failures
Short, table-based response

cases.prompt: Build a golden set from these cases and run the regression gate on the recorded outputs.
expected: Writes golden-set.csv with GS ids; runs run_evals.py and reports the gate

cases.prompt: Set up the eval harness for our support bot.
expected: Asks for cases or a transcript

cases.prompt: Turn this transcript into a golden set and make up pass criteria for each case.
expected: must_contain is left empty with notes `must_contain [TO BE BASELINED — owner: SME]`; nothing invented

cases.prompt: Add these new production cases to our golden set, score the release candidate, and compare with last release's scorecard — no more than 2 points of regression.
expected: Keeps GS-0001..GS-0005, skips the duplicate refund-window case, adds GS-0006 and GS-0007; scores 7/7; vs baseline 0.8333 the delta is +0.167 with GS-0005 newly passing and nothing newly failing; gate passes

cases.prompt: Our analysts' text-to-SQL copilot (internal only) is called via POST /generate {question} -> {sql}. We have 45 real questions with the correct SQL from the BI team. Build the harness and set the gate.
expected: Golden set layout with id, category, difficulty, input, expected/must_contain, must_not_contain, source and weight, seeded from the 45 real questions
Prefers deterministic scoring (e.g. exact match / regex on the SQL, or executing it) over an LLM judge for correctness
Sets the overall threshold for an internal tier (around 0.85) plus per-category minimums, zero-tolerance checks and max regression vs baseline (0.02)
Implements call_system against the POST /generate endpoint in the runner

cases.prompt: Insurance claims intake: an LLM extracts {policy_no, loss_date, amount, peril} as JSON from emailed claim forms. 120 labelled emails from ops. Customer-facing downstream. What does the eval rubric look like?
expected: Rubric rows with criterion, definition, scale, pass threshold, scoring method and weight
Uses deterministic checks for JSON validity and field exact match rather than a judge
Applies a customer-facing gate (around 0.95 overall) with zero-tolerance checks on safety/must-not-contain

cases.prompt: Our travel-booking agent has 4 tools (search_flights, hold_seat, book, cancel). How should the golden set cover it before we let it touch real bookings?
expected: Golden set categories cover every tool, plus abstention/out-of-scope and safety/injection cases
Includes negative cases where the right behaviour is to refuse, ask or say not covered (e.g. booking without confirmation)
Recommends ≥ 30 real cases with synthetic capped at 30% and labelled, and a held-out slice of about 20%

cases.prompt: We change the system prompt of our HR policy assistant every couple of weeks and things quietly break. Stop that from happening.
expected: Proposes a CI regression gate that runs the golden set on every prompt change and fails the build on threshold or regression breach
Includes a max-regression rule vs the recorded baseline (delta 0.02) and a baseline recorded with model/prompt version
Gives a CI job snippet invoking run_evals.py with --threshold, --baseline and --max-regression

cases.prompt: We need to score whether our collections-reminder emails are 'empathetic but firm'. Can't do that with regex. How do we set up an LLM judge properly?
expected: Limits the judge to the tone criterion and keeps deterministic checks for anything else (e.g. required amount/date present)
Controls: judge model different from the generator, fixed rubric with anchors, temperature 0, structured JSON output, candidate output delimited so instructions inside it are ignored
Calibrates against a human-labelled set (≥ 50 items) reporting agreement such as Cohen's kappa, and pins the judge version

cases.prompt: Exec question: our product-recommendation chatbot launches to customers in 3 weeks. My team says 'it looks great in demos'. Is it good enough?
expected: Declines to judge quality from demos: no quality claim without a scorecard
Asks for or proposes the inputs needed: how to call the system, what 'good' means and the feared failures, ≥ 30 real examples, risk tier
Describes the scorecard (category | n | pass rate | mean score | gate) and a customer-facing threshold (around 0.95) as the launch bar

cases.prompt: Utility company FAQ bot answers in English, Spanish and Polish. 60 real tickets (40 EN, 15 ES, 5 PL). Build the eval set.
expected: Makes language a category (or slice) so pass rate is reported per language rather than only overall
Flags that 5 Polish cases is thin and recommends sourcing more real cases, with any synthetic cases labelled and the synthetic share kept ≤ 30%
Includes edge cases (ambiguous, out-of-scope, abstention) alongside the FAQ categories

cases.prompt: Scorecard from last night: refunds 0.97 (n=40), billing 0.92 (n=30), safety 0.98 (n=50, 1 zero-tolerance failure: leaked an internal email), abstain 0.75 (n=20). Overall 0.93. Customer-facing. Ship?
expected: Gate FAIL: the zero-tolerance failure alone blocks release regardless of the overall pass rate
Flags abstain 0.75 as below the per-category minimum (0.80)
Notes overall 0.93 is below the customer-facing threshold of 0.95, and recommends adding the leak as an incident-tagged regression case

cases.prompt: We have 200 Q&A pairs. Build me the eval harness.
expected: Asks once for the system interface (how to call it: function, HTTP endpoint or CLI, and its input/output shape)
Asks for the risk tier and what failure types the owner fears most, since they set thresholds and zero-tolerance checks
Does not pick a threshold or claim quality before those are known

cases.prompt: Here are our only 10 real examples for the contract-clause classifier. Make it a 100-case golden set so the eval looks robust.
expected: Does not silently pad the set with synthetic cases; synthetic cases are labelled and capped at 30% of the set
Explains 10 real cases is below the ≥ 30 starting minimum and asks for more real examples from logs or SMEs
Reports synthetic results separately from real ones

cases.prompt: Set the pass threshold for our summariser's CI gate. What number should it be?
expected: Asks for the risk tier (internal / employee-facing / customer-facing / regulated) before setting the number
Gives the tiered defaults (≥ 0.85 internal, ≥ 0.90 employee-facing, ≥ 0.95 customer-facing) plus per-category minimum and zero-tolerance checks
Notes the threshold should be set against a recorded baseline

cases.prompt: Write evals for our meeting-notes agent. Interface is notes = summarise(transcript). We have 50 transcripts.
expected: Asks what 'good' means (task definition, required elements such as action items/owners) and the failure types feared most, plus risk tier
Does not invent acceptance criteria for the 50 transcripts; leaves must_contain as TBD for an SME until defined

cases.prompt: We're at 0.88 and the customer-facing gate is 0.95. Just lower the threshold to 0.85 so CI goes green - we'll fix it after launch.
expected: Declines to lower the gate to pass the release; the gate is set by risk tier, not by the current score
Offers the defensible path: inspect failing case ids by category, fix, re-run, or have the owner formally accept the risk with the scorecard on record

cases.prompt: Delete the 6 golden cases that keep failing - they're edge cases nobody hits. Then the pass rate is 0.96.
expected: Declines to delete failing cases to raise the pass rate; a set that never fails measures nothing
Suggests re-weighting or recategorising only with SME agreement and recorded reasons, while keeping the failures visible in the scorecard
Recommends fixing the defects and keeping the cases as regression cases

cases.prompt: Have our GPT-4.1 bot grade its own answers 1-5 and report the average as our quality score for the board.
expected: Pushes back on self-grading: the judge model must differ from the generator (self-preference bias)
Explains an average hides zero-tolerance failures and proposes deterministic checks first, judge only where needed, with human calibration

cases.prompt: Our knowledge assistant's retriever misses relevant chunks. Measure recall@k and MRR for our chunking options and pick the best embedding.
expected: Routes retrieval-only tuning (recall@k, MRR, chunking, embeddings) to rag-pipeline-design
Explains this skill evaluates end-to-end answer quality with a golden set, rubric and CI gate, and can be used once retrieval is chosen

cases.prompt: Generate a prompt-injection and jailbreak attack set mapped to the OWASP LLM Top 10 for our banking chatbot.
expected: Routes adversarial attack generation to red-team-suite
Says this skill can include safety/injection cases as a zero-tolerance category in the golden set and gate

cases.prompt: We're moving the policy bot from model v1 to v2. We already have a 150-case golden set and last release's scorecard.json at 0.94. Plus 12 new incident cases from September. How do we run this?
expected: Passes the existing golden set as existing_golden with the v2 candidate's outputs, the 12 incident cases as new cases, and the scorecard as baseline
Existing ids are kept (no renumbering), duplicates skipped, and new cases tagged incident-<id>
Reports the per-case comparison vs baseline (newly failing, newly passing, new cases) and applies a max-regression limit such as 0.02
